sentences.text:
The facts of the case in short are as under:
2- The applicant is a Private Limited Company engaged in the E-commerce business of trading and supplying genetically modified seeds, fertilizers and other agricultural inputs directly from wholesalers/manufacturers/ producers across India.

The applicant entered into an agreement with Vikas Enterprises for the purpose of storage of its products located at 17-A, Vikas Bhawan, Udoyg Nagar, Nemawar Road,
Palda, Indore.

3- The complainant Satyanarayan Jat from the office of Senior Agricultural Officer,
Block Indore submitted a written complaint in police Station Bhawankua Indore that he and the senior agricultural development officer conducted a raid on 15.02.2023 at New Diamond Transport, 19, Udyog Nagar Palda and found storage of large quantity of genetically modified seeds, fertilizers, pesticides and other agricultural inputs belonging to applicant valued Rs. 1 crore.
The sale and storage license of the applicant company had already expired on 03.10.2022.
Since there was no valid license hence all the materials were handed over on supurdginama to the applicant and the godown was sealed.

According to the complainant instead of storing the materials at 17- A, Vikas Bhawan, Udoyg Nagar,
Nemawar Road, Palda, Indore and all goods which were found at 19, Udyog Nagar Palda which is in violation of Section 29(1) (b), 29 (1) (c) and 29(1) (d) of the Insecticides Act, 1968.
The FIR No.291/2023 has been registered under the aforesaid section and 420 of IPC against Avi Jain and Mukul Garg on 22.02.2023.

- : 3 :-
4- Both the accused applied for anticipatory bail under Section 438 of the Cr.P.C.
which has been granted by Additional Sessions Judge vide order dated 08.04.2023.

5- The applicant filed an application for the release of seized material and removal of the seal under Section 451 and 457 of Cr.P.C. before the Judicial Magistrate First Class which came to be dismissed vide order dated 19.04.2023 that the sealed samples were sent to the FSL and the report has not been received till date.
Being aggrieved by the aforesaid order a revision was filed which was also dismissed vide order dated 10.05.2023 hence, this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. before this Court.

sentences.text: Shri Shantanu Sharma learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant company is having licenses to store and sell insecticides, pesticides and agriculture inputs in other states also.
There are no allegations in the FIR that these seized materials are not meeting the standards prescribed under the Insecticides Act, 1968.
That large quantity of insecticides, pesticides and agriculture inputs have been only seized because it was found stored without a license at a place other than mentioned in the agreement.
The applicant is ready to shift these materials to another place where the applicant is having valid licenses like State of Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Maharashtra.
It is further submitted that these materials were stored not for sale in Indore but only for transportation to other states.
The value of these goods is crores of rupees and losing their shelf life day by day.
As on today, the applicant has suffered a loss of Rs.35,00,000/- as the material has expired its shelf life, therefore, the same may kindly be released.

The prosecution agency is not in a position to get the report from - : 4 :-
the lab in the near future.
6- Learned Government Advocate for the respondent / State was directed to obtain instructions.

Learned Government Advocate submits that the seized materials cannot be released to the applicant as the applicant has no license to store in Indore however, he has agreed that the applicant can be permitted to shift and store these materials at a licensed store.
7- In view of the above, the material belonging to the applicant were seized on 15.03.2023 and till date, the FSL report has not been received.
There is no allegation in the FIR that these insecticides and pesticides are not meeting the standards prescribed under the Act.

The only allegation is that these were stored at different place without a license, therefore, the respondents are directed to remove the seal and release the insecticides, pesticides and agriculture inputs to the applicant.
The applicant is directed to transfer these materials to a place where the license to store is there.

The entire release and shifting be done under the supervision of a complainant or Senior Agriculture Officer within a period of three days from today from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
With the aforesaid, the present petition is partly allowed.
(VIVEK RUSIA) JUDGE praveen.
